newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 25.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Domestic banks announced another decrease in interest rates today. Komercni Banka will decrease its reference rate to 18.6 percent and its base rate to 16.5 percent. CSOB decreased its base rate for credits of up to one year to 21 percent. Banka Hana's reference rate is 22 percent from today.

- Former Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik became a member of the board of directors of the largest insurance company in the country, Ceska Pojistovna. According to sources, the group PPF, which owns the insurance company is behind Kocarnik's entering this position.
- The Czech National Bank was not consulted over the issue of nine billion crowns worth of bonds planned by the city of Prague. The central bank considers this idea macroeconomically harmful.
- President Vaclav Havel should begin discussions on NATO membership tomorrow with coalition and opposition parties.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Finance Ministry's the capital market office decided to begin forced administration in Investicni Fond Prace a Podnikani for allegedly violating the law on investment companies, which harmed the interests of shareholders.

- From August 1, members of the Prague Stock Exchange will be able to trade with securities only on the premisise of this institution or at RM-System, not through the Securities Centre, where about half of all transactions take place now.

- According to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, the latest statistics on domestic economic development are witness to the fact that the situation in the country will not be as dramatic as it seemed. He said the key task for the near future is to maintain political stability.
- The central bank decreased its repo rate yesterday to 18.5 percent from 20, and the crown rose.

- Economic ministers yesterday approved an energy policy for the Czech Republic, which plans on progressively creating competition in energy. Industry and Trade Minister Karel Kuhnl expects prices to double by the year 2000.
- Union Group obtained permission from the National Bank of Poland to enter Prumyslova Banka. The group should obtain 66 percent of shares in two months.

- The 14th NATO conference ended yesterday, and participating Eastern European politicians walked away expecting three new NATO members in the first wave. President Vaclav Havel presented a medal for the Order of the White Lion to American General George Joulwan.

PRAVO - The proposal from the leader of one faction in the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), Ivan Masek, to decrease income tax rates for legal persons from January 1 to 33 percent obtained the support of the Civic Democratic Party (ODS), but the Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL) are still undecided.

- Ticket prices on Czech Railways will most probably increase from October 1. The average increase is expected to be by 50 percent, although more for short connections and less for longer connections.
- In a general meeting on Tuesday, shareholders of Ceska Pojistovna approved audited losses of 5.2 billion crowns, for which reserves were created.
- CKD Praha signed a preliminary contract with American Lockheed Martin for cooperation between the two companies in manufacturing F-16 fighter aircrafts.

- Valcovny Trub, together with two other domestic manufacturers of iron seamless pipes, which are affected by antidumping export measures from the EU, will meet on Thursday with representatives of the European Commission on this issue.

LIDOVE NOVINY - According to estimates from the union of software manufacturers and distributors (BSA), about 80 percent of computer programmes currently used in the Czech Republic are pirate, causing damages to manufacturers last year of seven billion crowns.
- The cabinet should decide today whether it will approve the exchange of T-72 tanks for L-39 Aero Vodochody fighter jets with Algeria.
